text: Hey everybody, I'm Dan McClellan. I'm a
scholar of the Bible and religion and I
wanted to share something that I got in
the mail today from a friend of mine
named Robert Algot. Now previously
Robert had sent me a 3D printed model of
the Taanach cult stand and this is about
2/3 actual size and it in my opinion and
the opinion of other scholars is a model
shrine. It is intended to miniaturize
and mobilize the sacred space of a
shrine and I think it is also
functioning as an incense
altar. So incense would be burned on the
top there, but it would also function to
house a little mini divine image on the
inside and in my opinion and the opinion
of some other scholars, the four
different registers and the symbolism
within them probably represents a
goddess, probably Asherah. So this is my
second favorites artifact from ancient
Israel and Palestine, but today I got in
the mail a replica of my favorite
artifact of all time from ancient Israel
and Palestine and that is the Kuntillet
Ajrud Pithos A Adonai and his Asherah
drawing and inscription. And this is
something I've talked about many times
in the past, but in again my opinion and
the opinion of a number of other
scholars, the two figures on the left
represent Adonai, the god of Israel, and
their consort partner or wife Asherah
and the inscription that is centered
above the headdress of the male figure
says saying of so-and-so
say to Yaheli and Yo'asa, I have blessed
you two or by Adonai of Samaria which is
Samaria and two or by his Asherah. Now
there's been a lot of debate about
whether or not the inscription is
supposed to be connected with the
drawings and if his Asherah is supposed
to refer to a cultic object or to a
goddess. This is a really good paper by
a friend of mine that I think makes a
very compelling argument for
understanding the two figures as
representing Adonai and Asherah even
though they are drawn using Bes and
Beset imagery and this is I think one of
the coolest artifacts in the world. It
dates to about 800 BCE and is one of a
number of pieces of evidence that
suggests that prior to the 7th century
BCE, the god of Israel was probably
worshipped alongside their consort
partner or wife Asherah and I think the
Taanach cult stand is also supportive of
that. But I think this is the best
replica I've ever seen of the Kuntillet
Ajrud Pithos A inscription and drawing
of Adonai and his Asherah. So phenomenal
phenomenal work Robert. Robert has a
website called relics3d.com
where he's got both the Taanach cult
stand and the Pithos A drawing and
inscription models for sale as well as I
think the 3D renderings that you can
download if you want to try to print
them yourselves. So go check that out if
you're interested in replicas like this
of these ancient artifacts which I think
are very very cool. So thank you so much
Robert. This is incredibly kind of you
and again phenomenal phenomenal work.
And thank you everybody else for
watching. And the fit for this video
is DuckTales. Awoohoo!
